newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes firm amid talk of imports.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes firm amid talk of imports.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rose Tuesday despite talk that buyers would substitute South American crudees for Alaska this month, traders said.
A major West Coast refiner offered 900,000 barrels of Canadon Seco (Argentina) crude to other West Coast companies, traders said, declining to name the price.
One or two refiners could buy the cargo, which could load in late August and arrive to the West Coast in mid-September.
"They're trying to decide whether to bring it to the West Coast or not," a refinery trader said.
Regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, which last traded in the West Coast market in mid-June at $2.16 under benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, didn't trade Tuesday.
Spot prices rose in line with broader market gains, including a 50 cents a barrel rise in September spot WTI.
Traders said the main ANS seller, BP Oil, kept trying to sell at a $1.85 discount to WTI.
Traders said Maya (Mexican) crude and Oriente (Ecuador) crude would continue to come north in September,.
Loreto (Peru) crude could also run, traders said.
